mainTopic: Three 'אין בין' משניות: a full-benefit vow vs. a food-only vow, נדרים vs. נדבות, and a זב of two emissions vs. one of three.
overview: This amud goes through three more משניות in the 'אין בין' series, each naming just one difference between two cases. First, a מודר הנאה differs from a מודר מאכל only in walking on the friend's land and borrowing non-food utensils. רבא explains that the ban on walking follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids even ויתור. Next, נדרים and נדבות differ only in the duty to replace a lost animal, though בל תאחר applies to both. A נדר ('הרי עלי') is like a load on your shoulders, so you must replace it, while a נדבה ('הרי זו') is tied only to that animal. Finally, a זב with two emissions and one with three differ only in the קרבן. The גמרא proves this from רבי סימאי's two פסוקים together with the word מזובו, and explains why both sources are needed. It then shows that the other מזובו teaches that a זב with two emissions must also count seven clean days. The amud ends as the ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed when logic seems to teach this.

steps.title: Full-benefit vow vs. food-only vow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the only differences between a מודר הנאה and a מודר מאכל are stepping on the friend's property and using his non-food utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The only difference between someone forbidden by vow to get any benefit from his friend, and someone forbidden by vow to get food from him, is walking on his property and using his utensils that are not used for preparing food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares two kinds of vows and says they differ in only two things: walking on the other person's land, and borrowing utensils that are not used for food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מודר הנאה is forbidden every kind of benefit, so walking on the land and borrowing non-food utensils are forbidden to him. A מודר מאכל is only forbidden food-related benefit, so those two things are allowed to him. Everything else is treated the same for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'
'There is no difference between' (the formula of this whole series of משניות)
Someone forbidden by a vow from getting any benefit from a certain person
Someone forbidden by a vow only from that person's food
Stepping foot, meaning walking across someone's property
Food preparation, literally 'food for the soul'

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's two questions: what we learn about food utensils, and why walking on land counts as benefit at all.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: There is no difference between
one forbidden by vow from benefiting from his fellow
and one forbidden by vow from his food,
except stepping foot (on his property)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵלִים שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין בָּהֶן אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ.
phrases.english: and utensils that are not used to prepare food.
phrases.notes: He means borrowing these utensils. They are forbidden to the first person but allowed to the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ לַמּוּדָּר מִמֶּנּוּ מַאֲכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of 'אין בין' משניות in this פרק with a new pair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מודר הנאה is forbidden to walk on his friend's property and to borrow his non-food utensils; a מודר מאכל is allowed both. Otherwise they are the same.

steps.title: Food utensils are forbidden to both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the משנה's wording that utensils used for food are forbidden to both kinds of vower.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that regarding utensils used to prepare food, both people are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely: since the משנה only listed non-food utensils as a difference, food utensils must be forbidden to both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the person who only vowed off food may not borrow a pot or a knife used for cooking, because those utensils are counted as part of food benefit. So the line between the two vows is drawn at whether the utensil is connected to food.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא, the discussion of the משנה
'This implies', used to draw an inference
'This one and that one are equal'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the מודר מאכל may borrow anything that isn't actual food. Utensils used for food count as food benefit and are forbidden to him too.

phrases.english: GEMARA: This implies that regarding utensils
that are used to prepare food,
this one and that one are equal.
phrases.notes: Both the full-benefit vower and the food-only vower are forbidden to borrow them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְעִנְיַן כֵּלִים שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בָּהֶן אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from what the משנה did not list as a difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Utensils used for preparing food are forbidden to both the מודר הנאה and the מודר מאכל.

steps.title: Why is walking on land a benefit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: people don't care if others walk on their land, so why is it forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: Stepping foot? But people are not particular about that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why walking across someone's land is forbidden to the מודר הנאה, since owners normally don't mind it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something people freely allow everyone to do doesn't seem like a real benefit from the owner. So it is hard to see why the vow should forbid it. This sets up רבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Are particular, mind, care about
People

phrases.english: Stepping foot?
But people are not particular about that!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרִיסַת הָרֶגֶל? הָא לָא קָפְדִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first item the משנה listed and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a מודר הנאה may not walk on his friend's property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Owners don't mind people walking on their land, so it shouldn't count as a benefit forbidden by the vow.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids even things people normally let go of.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אליעזר, who said that things people let go of are forbidden to someone forbidden by vow from benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by saying this משנה follows the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that ויתור, a benefit people normally don't mind giving, is still forbidden to a מודר הנאה. Walking on land is exactly that kind of benefit, so by his view it is forbidden. The question assumed people's indifference makes it permitted; רבא shows that only fits a different view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose opinion is this?', used to tie a source to one תנא
Something people let go of, a benefit owners don't mind giving

steps.whatToRemember: Walking on someone's land is forbidden to a מודר הנאה only according to רבי אליעזר, who says even ויתור counts as forbidden benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's ruling on walking across land depends on one specific view about ויתור, not a rule everyone agrees on.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whose opinion is this? Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: something people let go of is forbidden
phrases.notes: ויתור is a small benefit owners normally don't mind giving, like walking through their field.

phrases.english: for one forbidden by vow from benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the משנה follows one specific תנא, רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since people don't mind others walking on their land, it should not count as forbidden benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אליעזר, even ויתור is forbidden to a מודר הנאה, so walking on the land is forbidden.

steps.title: Vow offerings vs. gift offerings
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says the only difference between נדרים and נדבות is that for a נדר you must replace the offering if it is lost or dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The only difference between vow offerings and gift offerings is that for vow offerings a person is responsible to replace them, and for gift offerings he is not responsible to replace them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה in the 'אין בין' series compares two kinds of קרבנות and names one difference: who must replace a lost offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a נדר animal dies or is lost before it is brought, the owner must bring another one. If a נדבה animal dies or is lost, he does not have to replace it. In every other way the two offerings are treated the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow offerings
Gift offerings
Responsibility, here the duty to replace a lost or dead offering
Obligated

steps.confusionAlert: Both are voluntary offerings. The difference is in how the person committed. With a נדר he took on an obligation himself ('I take upon myself an offering'). With a נדבה he only set aside this specific animal ('this animal is an offering').

phrases.english: MISHNAH: There is no difference between vow offerings and gift offerings,
except that for vow offerings one is responsible for them,
phrases.notes: Responsible means that if the animal dies or is lost before it is brought, he must replace it.

phrases.english: and for gift offerings one is not responsible for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה in the same 'אין בין' chain, moving from personal vows to קרבנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must replace a lost or dead נדר offering but not a lost or dead נדבה offering.

steps.title: Both kinds of offering share the rule against delay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads our משנה closely: since it lists only replacement as the difference, the law of בל תאחר must apply equally to a נדר and a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that for the rule of 'do not delay,' both are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a careful reading of the משנה from Step 5. It concludes that the rule against delaying applies to both kinds of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the 'only' difference is replacing a lost animal. So any other rule, like בל תאחר (not delaying a promised offering), must apply the same way to both. This is the same kind of reading from the משנה's wording that the גמרא used in Step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against delaying the fulfillment of a pledge to the בית המקדש
Both this and that are equal

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that regarding 'do not delay'
both this and that are equal.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means a נדר and a נדבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal inference from the wording of the משנה in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בל תאחר applies equally to both נדרים and נדבות.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere defines a נדר and a נדבה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה from another place explains that a נדר is 'הרי עלי עולה' and a נדבה is 'הרי זו עולה'. If the animal is lost, a נדר must be replaced but a נדבה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: What is a נדר? Someone who says, 'I take upon myself to bring an עולה.' What is a נדבה? Someone who says, 'This animal is an עולה.' What is the difference between them? With נדרים, if the animals died, were stolen, or were lost, he must replace them. With נדבות, if they died, were stolen, or were lost, he does not have to replace them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another place that explains exactly what a נדר and a נדבה are. It is setting up the question that comes next: where does this difference come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר is a personal promise ('on me'), so the obligation stays with the person until an offering is brought. A נדבה dedicates one specific animal ('this one'), so the obligation is tied only to that animal. This explains the replacement difference that our משנה mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is upon me': the wording of a נדר, a personal obligation
'This is': the wording of a נדבה, which dedicates a specific animal
Responsibility to replace something if it is lost
A burnt-offering

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix them up. נדר = 'עלי' (on ME, so I must replace it). נדבה = 'זו' (THIS animal, so if it is gone, I owe nothing).

phrases.english: We learned there:
Which is a vow offering?
One who says: 'It is upon me to bring a burnt-offering.'
Which is a gift offering?
One who says: 'This animal is a burnt-offering.'
And what is the difference between vow offerings and gift offerings?

phrases.aramaic: נְדָרִים, מֵתוּ אוֹ נִגְנְבוּ אוֹ אָבְדוּ
phrases.english: Vow offerings: if they died, were stolen, or were lost
he is responsible to replace them.

phrases.aramaic: נְדָבוֹת, מֵתוּ אוֹ נִגְנְבוּ אוֹ אָבְדוּ
phrases.english: Gift offerings: if they died, were stolen, or were lost
he is not responsible to replace them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה that defines the terms from Step 5 and spells out the replacement difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדר ('עלי') must be replaced if lost. A נדבה ('זו') does not.

steps.title: What is the source for the replacement rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a נדר must be replaced but a נדבה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the difference it just learned. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the rule. The גמרא simply wants to know which פסוק teaches that only a נדר carries responsibility to replace the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the rule stated in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a נדר must be replaced and a נדבה need not be.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns it from the words 'to atone upon him'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק 'ונרצה לו לכפר עליו'. רבי שמעון explains that an offering which is 'upon him' must be replaced, and one which is not 'upon him' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'And it shall be accepted for him to atone upon him.' רבי שמעון says: what is upon him, he must replace. What is not upon him, he does not have to replace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. רבי שמעון learns the difference from the word עליו ('upon him') in the פסוק about an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads עליו as describing an offering that is a burden on the person himself. That fits a נדר, which must be replaced. A נדבה was never placed 'on him', so he has no duty to replace it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it shall be accepted for him to atone upon him' (ויקרא א:ד)
That which is upon him, a personal obligation

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'And it shall be accepted for him to atone upon him,'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in ויקרא א:ד and talks about an עולה. The key word is עליו, 'upon him.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
That which is upon him, he is responsible to replace it;

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָלָיו — אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ.
phrases.english: and that which is not upon him, he is not responsible to replace it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's question with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word עליו in ויקרא א:ד teaches that only an offering the person took 'upon himself' must be replaced.

steps.title: How does the פסוק show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the word עליו actually points to a personal responsibility to replace the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון reads this idea into the פסוק. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a simple reading, 'to atone upon him' is about atonement, not about replacing a lost animal. So the גמרא wants to know how the word עליו is connected to responsibility.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the implication? How does it show this?

phrases.english: From where may this be inferred?
phrases.notes: He means: how does the word 'upon him' in the פסוק show that he must replace it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the פסוק in Step 9 shows the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word עליו shows a duty to replace the offering.

steps.title: Saying 'on me' is like carrying it on your shoulders
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי explains that someone who says 'עלי' is like a person carrying the offering on his own shoulders. It is his personal burden until he delivers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: Since he said 'on me,' it is as if he is carrying it on his shoulders.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי answers how the word עליו teaches responsibility. Saying 'on me' means taking on a load you must carry until it arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words עלי and עליו mean 'on me' and 'on him,' like a load resting on someone. Just as a porter stays responsible until the load is delivered, the נודר stays obligated until an offering is actually brought. That is why he must replace an animal that died or got lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he said
Who carries it on his shoulders
It is considered like

steps.whatToRemember: A נדר ('עלי') is a personal load on your shoulders, so you must replace a lost animal. A נדבה ('זו') is tied only to that animal, so you need not replace it. Both are included in בל תאחר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This picture of the 'load on the shoulders' is the basic reason behind every law of אחריות for נדרים versus נדבות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said:
Since he said 'upon me,'
it is considered as if he carries it on his shoulders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by explaining the meaning of עליו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עלי' means taking on a burden as if it were carried on one's shoulders, which brings a duty to replace a lost offering.

steps.title: Two emissions versus three: only the offering differs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a זב who sees two emissions and a זב who sees three differ only in the obligation to bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The only difference between a זב who sees two emissions and one who sees three is the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה in the 'אין בין' series. It says the only difference between a זב with two emissions and a זב with three is that the one with three brings a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'אין בין' style always names one difference and hides a big point: everything else is the same. Here the single difference is the קרבן that the three-emission זב brings when he becomes טהור. The גמרא will spell out what 'everything else' includes.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who has a special discharge that makes him טמא
A 'seeing', meaning one emission of the discharge
An offering brought in the בית המקדש
'There is no difference between', the opening formula of this series of משניות

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין זָב הָרוֹאֶה שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת
phrases.english: There is no difference between a zav who sees two emissions
and one who sees three, except for an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין זָב הָרוֹאֶה שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת לָרוֹאֶה שָׁלֹשׁ אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה in the same 'אין בין' series, moving from offerings that are נדר or נדבה to the laws of a זב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב with two emissions and a זב with three differ only in the obligation to bring a קרבן.

steps.title: Inference: in all other laws they are equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and infers that both types of זב are equal for making lying and sitting surfaces טמא and for counting seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that for lying surfaces, sitting surfaces, and counting seven days, both are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what the משנה implies: other than the קרבן, the two-emission זב and the three-emission זב have the same laws. It names three of those laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה names only the קרבן as a difference, everything else must be shared. Both cases make a bed or seat טמא, and both must count seven clean days before becoming טהור. This sets up the next question: where do we learn this?

keyTerms.meaning: A surface used for lying, which a זב makes טמא
A surface used for sitting, which a זב makes טמא
Counting seven clean days before he can become טהור
'This and that are equal'

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that regarding a surface for lying and a surface for sitting
and the counting of seven clean days,
this one and that one are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְעִנְיַן מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב וּסְפִירַת שִׁבְעָה זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the משנה implies about all the laws other than the קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both types of זב are equal for making lying and sitting surfaces טמא and for counting seven clean days.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that two emissions bring טומאה while only three bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack on the rule. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק tells us that two emissions are enough for טומאה but not for a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these words?', a standard request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source of the rule stated in the משנה and the inference from it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source showing that two emissions bring טומאה and three bring a קרבן.

steps.title: רבי סימאי: two for impurity, three for the offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי סימאי notes that one פסוק counts two emissions and calls the זב טמא, and another counts three and also calls him טמא. So two are for טומאה and three are for the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: רבי סימאי says: The Torah counted two and called him טמא. It counted three and called him טמא. How can that be? Two are for טומאה and three are for the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי סימאי shows that the Torah calls the זב טמא after two emissions and also after three, so the third emission must teach something extra: the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two emissions already make him טמא, the Torah has no need to say that three make him טמא. So the mention of three must add a new law, the obligation to bring a קרבן. That gives us the משנה's rule: טומאה starts at two, and the קרבן starts at three.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק counted'
Ritually impure
'How is this?', used to settle two sources that seem to overlap

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah source behind the משנה. It also shows a common way of learning: when the Torah seems to repeat itself, the repetition teaches a new law.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Simai says:
The verse counted two emissions and called him 'impure.'
phrases.notes: This is ויקרא טו:ב, which mentions the discharge twice and then says he is טמא.

phrases.english: It counted three and called him 'impure.'
phrases.notes: This is the next פסוק, ויקרא טו:ג, which mentions the discharge three times and again calls him טמא.

phrases.english: How so?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the Torah needs three if two are already enough to make him טמא.

phrases.english: Two are for impurity, and three are for the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah calls the זב טמא both after two emissions and after three. So two set up טומאה, and three add the obligation of a קרבן.

steps.title: Maybe the two cases are completely separate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reading: two emissions bring only טומאה and no קרבן, and three bring only a קרבן and no טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: two are for טומאה and not for a קרבן, and three are for a קרבן and not for טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי סימאי's reading. It suggests that each number might have its own law, so a man with three emissions would bring a קרבן but would not be טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי סימאי's split could be read as two separate groups instead of building on each other. Under that reading, a man with three emissions would bring a קרבן but would not have the טומאה laws at all. That would go against the inference in step 13 that both types are equal for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And say instead', offering a different reading

phrases.english: But say instead: two are for impurity and not for an offering,
three are for an offering and not for impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the ברייתא's split should be understood.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי סימאי's reading that three emissions bring a קרבן in addition to טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים could instead be dividing the laws between the two cases, so that three emissions bring only a קרבן and no טומאה.

steps.title: Anyone who saw three already saw two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: before he saw three emissions, he had already seen two, so he is already טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: before he saw three, he already saw two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the suggestion makes no sense, because three emissions always include two. So a man with three is טמא as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot reach three without first passing through two. Once he saw two, he was already טמא, and a third emission cannot take that טומאה away. So three adds the קרבן on top of טומאה, which confirms the משנה and the inference in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can say', introducing an obvious answer
'Before'

steps.whatToRemember: Two emissions make a זב טמא, with lying and sitting surfaces and seven clean days. Three emissions add a קרבן, because anyone who saw three has already seen two.

phrases.english: You can say: before he saw three,
he had already seen two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרַתְּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה שָׁלֹשׁ רָאָה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with simple logic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical answer: three emissions always include two.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each number might carry its own separate law, so three would bring a קרבן but no טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three emissions build on two. A man with three is טמא just like a man with two, and he also brings a קרבן.

steps.title: Maybe two emissions bring a קרבן and three bring טומאה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another possible reading of רבי סימאי's two פסוקים: two emissions require a קרבן but bring no טומאה, and three bring טומאה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say instead: two emissions are for a קרבן and not for טומאה, and three are also for טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to split the two פסוקים of רבי סימאי. This time two emissions give only a קרבן, and three give טומאה on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer (step 17) only blocked a reading where three emissions bring no טומאה. This new reading avoids that problem, because here three do bring טומאה. So the גמרא needs a new source to rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: And say instead (introduces a different possible reading)
An offering brought in the בית המקדש
Also, as well

phrases.english: And say instead: two emissions are for an offering
and not for impurity; three are also for impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 rejected one reversed reading, this offers a different reversed reading that step 17's logic does not block.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי סימאי's split: two emissions for טומאה, three for a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two פסוקים could just as easily be split so that two emissions bring a קרבן without טומאה, and three bring טומאה along with the קרבן.

steps.title: A ברייתא on מזובו: only some זבים bring a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion using a ברייתא. The word מזובו ('from his emission') teaches that some זבים bring a קרבן and some do not: three emissions bring one, two do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, as a ברייתא teaches: 'And the כהן shall make atonement for him before ה׳ from his emission.' Some זבים bring a קרבן and some do not. How so? If he saw three, he brings one. If he saw two, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the suggestion is impossible and quotes a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows from a פסוק that a זב with three emissions brings a קרבן and a זב with two does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The little word 'from' (מִן) in מזובו means 'only part of,' so not every זב brings a קרבן. The ברייתא says the ones who bring it are those with three emissions. That directly contradicts the suggestion that two emissions bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible
From his emission (ויקרא טו:טו)
Some, part of
How so? (asks for the details)

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind,
as it is taught: "And the priest shall make atonement for him
before the Lord from his emission"
phrases.notes: The key is the word "from." It hints at "some of," meaning not every זב.

phrases.english: some זבים bring an offering
and some זבים do not bring an offering.
How so?
If he saw three emissions, he brings one;
if he saw two, he does not bring one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by bringing an outside ברייתא that rules out its reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source (ברייתא on the word מזובו) that rules out the suggested reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two emissions might bring a קרבן without טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: מזובו shows that only some זבים bring a קרבן: three emissions bring one, two do not.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks: maybe two bring a קרבן and three do not
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, a challenge: maybe 'some bring, some don't' means the opposite, that two emissions bring a קרבן and three do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it means only this: if he saw two, he brings a קרבן; if he saw three, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. 'Some bring and some don't' could be split the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מזובו only tells us that some זבים are left out. It does not say which group, so the ברייתא checks whether the reversed split could work.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it means only this (raises the opposite reading)
He brings (a קרבן)

phrases.english: Or perhaps it means nothing other than:
if he saw two emissions, he brings an offering;
if he saw three, he does not bring one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא questions its own split from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's split: three emissions bring a קרבן, two do not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Some bring, some don't' does not say which group brings, so the split could be reversed.

steps.title: Whoever saw three already saw two
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the reversal: anyone who saw three emissions already saw two first, so three cannot bring less than two.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: before he saw three, he already saw two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the reversed reading with simple logic. Three emissions include two, so a man with three cannot be exempt if a man with two is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two emissions required a קרבן, someone with three would also have two and would have to bring it. Then no זב at all would be exempt, which goes against 'some do not bring.' So the only split that works is three bring and two do not. This is the same logic as step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: You can say (introduces the rebuttal)
Before (literally, 'until he had not yet')

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא on מזובו proves that two emissions bring no קרבן and three do. A reversed split fails because three always includes two.

phrases.english: You can say: before he saw three,
he already saw two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרַתְּ: עַד שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה שָׁלֹשׁ רָאָה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's own challenge from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical rebuttal: the larger number includes the smaller
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two emissions might bring a קרבן while three do not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three emissions always include two, so the reversal is impossible. Three bring a קרבן, two do not.

steps.title: Why we need both רבי סימאי and מזובו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each source covers a gap in the other. רבי סימאי gives the numbers, and מזובו rules out the suggestion from step 18.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both רבי סימאי's teaching and מזובו are needed. With only רבי סימאי, I would have read it like our question, so מזובו teaches otherwise. With only מזובו, I would not know how many emissions count, so רבי סימאי teaches that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain why it needed two separate sources for this one rule. It shows what each source adds that the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי סימאי's two פסוקים give the numbers two and three, but they could be split the wrong way, as in step 18. מזובו shows that only some זבים bring a קרבן, but by itself it gives no numbers. Put together, they give the full rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
I would have thought (the mistaken first idea)
It teaches us (otherwise)
Sightings, emissions seen

steps.whatToRemember: רבי סימאי gives the numbers (two and three). מזובו tells us which number brings the קרבן. We need both.

phrases.english: It was necessary to cite רבי סימאי's teaching
and it was necessary to cite "from his emission,"
because if we had only רבי סימאי's teaching,
I would have said it works like our question,
phrases.notes: "Our question" is step 18: two bring a קרבן, and three bring טומאה too.

phrases.english: so "from his emission" teaches us otherwise.
And if we had only "from his emission,"
I would not know how many emissions it takes,
so רבי סימאי's teaching tells us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sources have been brought, this explains why neither one alone would be enough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sources are needed. רבי סימאי gives the numbers, and מזובו decides which number brings the קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא assumes the Torah does not repeat a teaching for nothing. When two sources seem to say the same thing, it shows what each one adds.

steps.title: What do we learn from the other מזובו?
steps.stepSummary: Since מזובו in one פסוק was used for a teaching, the גמרא asks what we learn from the same word in the earlier פסוק, 'when the זב is cleansed from his emission.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said 'from his emission' comes to teach something, what do you learn from 'And when the זב is cleansed from his emission'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question that the next step will answer. The word מזובו also appears in an earlier פסוק, so what does it teach there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we said the extra 'from' in מזובו (ויקרא טו:טו) teaches 'only some,' the same word in ויקרא טו:יג should also teach something. The גמרא wants to know what that teaching is.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that you have said
For a teaching (a lesson drawn from the wording)
What do you learn from it?

phrases.english: And now that you have said
that "from his emission" comes to teach something,
"And when the זב is cleansed from his emission"
phrases.notes: This is an earlier פסוק (ויקרא טו:יג) about the seven clean days. It has the same word מזובו.

phrases.english: what do you learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 19's teaching from מזובו and asks about the same word in another פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson comes from the word מזובו in ויקרא טו:יג, 'when the זב is cleansed from his emission'?

steps.title: The earlier מזובו is needed for a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the word מזובו in 'when the זב is cleansed from his emission' is needed for a ברייתא. That ברייתא teaches the זב counts once his emission stops, and his נגע does not hold him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: 'And when the זב is cleansed' means when his emission stops. 'From his emission' means only from his emission, not from his emission and his נגע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23. It shows that the word מזובו in the earlier פסוק has its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'cleansed from his emission' to mean the זב's emissions have stopped. Because the פסוק says only 'from his emission,' a זב who is also a מצורע does not need his נגע to heal before he starts counting. So this מזובו is busy with this teaching and does not repeat the other one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
As was taught in a ברייתא
When it stops
His נגע, his mark of צרעת

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not from his emission and his נגע' does not mean the נגע disappears. It only means the נגע does not stop him from counting his seven days for the זיבה.

phrases.english: That one is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: 'That one' means the word מזובו in the earlier פסוק, the one asked about in step 23.

phrases.english: "And when the זב is cleansed" —
when his emission stops,
["From his emission" —] and not from his emission and his נגע.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. He only needs his emission to stop, not his צרעת as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 23 about the purpose of the earlier מזובו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word מזובו in the earlier פסוק teaches.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that the זב counts once his emission stops, even if his נגע has not healed.

steps.title: A זב with two emissions also counts seven days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: from 'from his emission, then he shall count,' we learn that a זב who saw only two emissions also needs ספירת שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From his emission, then he shall count' teaches about a זב who had two emissions: he also needs to count seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns a second law from the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From earlier steps we know a זב of two emissions does not bring a קרבן. Someone might think he also skips ספירת שבעה. The פסוק teaches that he still must count seven clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting seven clean days
Two sightings (two emissions)
It taught

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for one of the shared laws the גמרא inferred in step 13. A זב of two emissions differs from one of three only in the קרבן, and both must count ספירת שבעה.

phrases.english: "From his emission, then he shall count" —

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת
phrases.english: it taught about a זב who had two emissions
that he requires a count of seven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִזּוֹבוֹ וְסָפַר לִימֵּד עַל זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second teaching from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב who saw two emissions must count seven clean days.

steps.title: Why is a פסוק needed if logic already teaches this?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges itself. A זב of two emissions already makes a משכב and מושב impure, so shouldn't logic alone tell us he must count seven days?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it logical? If he makes a bed and a seat impure, shouldn't he need to count seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed for the law in step 25. This question sets up the ברייתא's next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב of two emissions already has the strong impurity of a full זב: he makes the things he lies on and sits on impure. So it seems obvious that he would also need ספירת שבעה. If logic teaches it, the extra word in the פסוק would seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it logical? (we could figure it out by reasoning)
Makes impure
Something made for lying on
Something made for sitting on

phrases.english: But isn't it logical?
If he makes a bed and a seat impure,
phrases.notes: The subject is the זב of two emissions from the line before.

phrases.english: shouldn't he require a count of seven days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק used in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to learn from the פסוק that a זב of two emissions needs ספירת שבעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He already makes a משכב and מושב impure like a full זב, so logic should require ספירת שבעה without a פסוק.
